clue.text: Old-fashioned characters used to mark out enclosures

definitions.text: Old-fashioned characters used to mark out enclosures

parts.words: Old-fashioned characters used to mark out enclosures
parts.note: read one way, fogeyish people fencing off fields; read as typography, the printed symbols with right-angled corners that box off a passage of text

explanation.surface: Fuddy-duddy locals pacing out the boundaries of fenced paddocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old-fashioned' gives SQUARE (a fogey is a square) and the enclosures are bracketed insertions in text, so the whole clue reads both as quaint people and as punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: These punctuation marks enclose editorial insertions, the right-angled version of round parentheses.

clue.text: Quiet community in eerie castle may be an eye opener

indicators.note: in says one piece is put inside the other
something eerie is weird and unsettling, so the letters of castle are turned strange and rearranged

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for playing quietly
EC is the European Community

explanation.surface: A hushed village inside a spooky castle could be quite a revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eye opener' pretends to be a literal sight-aid (spectacles), but it means a surprising sight; 'eerie' rearranges the castle and 'in' sets the quiet community inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is a striking sight that makes people stare in astonishment.

clue.text: Give a lift to a group? Heavens, not all of it!

indicators.note: not all of it says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at being asked to carry a whole party, insisting they cannot manage everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave something up is to raise or hoist it.

clue.text: Avidly watch some games with a small winning margin

parts.note: a rubber is a set of games, as in bridge or cricket Tests
winning by a neck is a narrow victory in horse racing

explanation.surface: Sports fans glued to a series of closely fought contests.
explanation.walkthrough: A rubber is a series of games, a term from bridge and from cricket Test series.
explanation.definitionFit: To gawp or stare inquisitively at something, craning the head round.

clue.text: See 1
French article probes amendments like a working 16?

indicators.note: probes means one piece pushes into the middle of another

parts.note: riders are clauses added to a bill or verdict
les is the plural French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A French newspaper piece digs into proposed changes to the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is PERCHERON, a draught horse: one hauling a cart carries no one on its back.
explanation.definitionFit: A working carthorse pulls loads rather than carrying a person mounted on it.

clue.text: Food token

definitions.meaning: a gambling counter used in a casino

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a fried potato strip, and a counter standing for money at the gaming table.

clue.text: Choose artist to portray tragic heroine

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: Picking a painter to depict a doomed woman from drama.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek tragedy figure who urges her brother to avenge their murdered father Agamemnon.

clue.text: A vice we must get over, finding a source of strength

parts.note: a sin is a vice

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting over means turning upwards, so the word we is read from the bottom

explanation.surface: Overcoming a bad habit gives a person inner resilience.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendon, the cord of tissue that gives muscles their power.

clue.text: A little bird behaving busily?

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A small bird flitting about industriously.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hard at work on something, fully occupied.

clue.text: Show, once nearly a success, was gripping

parts.note: ex means former, once

indicators.note: nearly says the word is cut short of its last letter

parts.note: a hit is a success
bit is the past tense of bite, to grip with the teeth

explanation.surface: A theatre production that almost triumphed in its day held the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: To display something publicly, as in a gallery.

clue.text: One following doctor's route for blood bank perhaps?

indicators.note: following says the one comes after the doctor

parts.note: DR is short for doctor
I is the Roman numeral one
a vein carries blood back to the heart

explanation.surface: A patient trailing the doctor along the path to the blood donation centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blood bank' is the false phrase: the definition is just 'bank', a kind that serves customers in their cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank branch, cinema or restaurant designed so customers stay seated in their cars.

clue.text: Flight path rescheduled to carry jet

indicators.note: rescheduling rearranges something, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An aircraft's route is changed so it can transport a jet.
explanation.definitionFit: The curve followed by a projectile or aircraft through the air.

clue.text: Arrange for transportation from one point to another

parts.note: S is south, a compass point
W is west, another compass point

explanation.surface: Organising the shipping of goods from one place to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' means a point of the compass, so the clue spells S, TO, W.
explanation.definitionFit: To pack cargo away securely in a hold for the voyage.

clue.text: In a very sorry state-self-inflicted?

parts.note: a wretched condition one has brought on oneself suggests the guilt felt after doing wrong

explanation.surface: Someone in a dreadful mess they created themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of guilt and regret, a misery caused by one's own wrongdoing.

clue.text: Make a profit, investing what's spare in a trophy

indicators.note: investing in the sense of clothing or surrounding, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: a cup is a trophy
spare means thin or lean

explanation.surface: Putting surplus funds into a prize to turn a gain.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for making a big gain financially.

clue.text: One balancing on a horse

parts.note: a percher is someone or something perched, balancing

explanation.surface: A rider teetering on top of a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of heavy French draught animal, grey or black.

clue.text: It's nonsense, cutting down English trees

parts.note: the yew is a tree
the ash is another tree

explanation.surface: Someone protests that felling England's woodland is foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting down' only links: the pieces simply sit side by side, E then two trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Humbug or rubbish, talk designed to deceive.

clue.text: Mostly misty, a road's beginning to oppress us — it's risky

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word for misty

parts.note: hazy means misty
RD is short for road

indicators.note: beginning to says take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A foggy road starting to bear down on us is a danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Dangerous, carrying a chance of harm.

clue.text: The Tempter can be almost reticent

indicators.note: can be signals these letters can become a different arrangement
almost says the word reticent is used without its final letter

explanation.surface: The Devil might nearly be reserved.
explanation.definitionFit: One who lures or tempts, as Satan is the great tempter.

clue.text: Fish seen round two islands in this country

indicators.note: round says the fish surrounds the islands

parts.note: tuna is a fish
IS is an abbreviation for islands
I is short for island

explanation.surface: A fish is spotted circling a pair of islands in this North African state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two islands' gives IS and I, the two usual abbreviations for island.
explanation.definitionFit: The North African nation, here pointed to by the italicised 'this'.

clue.text: The stage one may reach in colloquial usage?

definitions.text: The stage one may reach in colloquial usage?

parts.words: The stage one may reach in colloquial usage?
parts.note: 'the stage' as a career, called by a slangy short name, rather than a phase someone reaches

explanation.definitionFit: The informal term for the entertainment industry, theatre and the like.

clue.text: Belt for fashionable laird in olden times

indicators.note: in places the reworked letters inside the other piece

parts.note: BC means before Christ, long ago

indicators.note: fashionable read as fashioned, made into a new shape, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A trendy Scottish landowner wore this strap in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: A laird is a Scottish landowner; 'fashionable' rearranges LAIRD to ALDRI, put 'in' BC.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash worn over the shoulder to carry a sword or bugle.

clue.text: Put under pressure for money by a king?

parts.note: to dun is to press a debtor for payment
K is king in chess

explanation.surface: A monarch squeezing his subjects for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put under pressure' looks like one phrase; the definition is 'Put under', as of a biscuit into tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To dip or plunge briefly into liquid, as with a biscuit in tea.

clue.text: Places to get rid of remains of depression?

definitions.text: Places to get rid of remains
definitions.meaning: tips where rubbish or leftovers are discarded
as in 'down in the', low spirits

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: rubbish tips, and gloom as in being down in them.

clue.text: Vessel catching fresh sole for a supplier

indicators.note: catching means the ship holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a whaler is a whaling ship

indicators.note: fresh suggests something newly made, so these letters are formed anew

explanation.surface: A fishing boat landing fresh flatfish to sell on to the trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader who sells goods in bulk to retailers.

clue.text: Look into each half of a joint

indicators.note: each half of says take the first half of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: Inspecting a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of meat from the lower back, such as pork or lamb.

clue.text: 10 + 10 turns up one — that follows

annotationWithheld.why: 10 + 10 turns up one — that follows (4): NEXT reads as X inside TEN, all reversed, but no clue word signals the insertion (only '+')

clue.text: One may be needing, say, a rubber

definitions.text: One may be needing, say, a rubber

parts.words: One may be needing, say, a rubber
parts.note: needing sounds like kneading, and a rubber is one who rubs, a therapist working on muscles

explanation.definitionFit: A man who gives massages, working muscles with the hands.

clue.text: Conclude by reflecting on first part of poem

indicators.note: by means beside, the next piece follows on

parts.note: to infer is to conclude

indicators.note: reflecting, as in a mirror, means the word on is read backwards

explanation.surface: Ending a reading with thoughts on the opening of a verse.
explanation.definitionFit: The first section of Dante's Divine Comedy, the journey through Hell.

clue.text: The way skill in this country secures aid to rapid progress?

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
art means skill
GB is Great Britain, the newspaper's own country
locks means secures

explanation.surface: A national talent for fastening things helps speed things along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this country' is GB from the viewpoint of a British paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprinters push off from these fixed footrests for a fast start.

clue.text: See 29
